title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride in Austin struck and killed a duck in the Mueller neighborhood while in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. The vehicle did not slow down or stop after the collision. This shows a perception or decision-making failure where the system did not recognize or react to an animal in its path, and it also shows a gap in the safety operator's ability or readiness to intervene in real time.

The failure occurred in a deployed service operating on public streets near a lake where wildlife was present. It would have been caught by testing that included scenarios with animals in roadways, or by operational boundaries that excluded areas with known animal activity until the system could handle such situations reliably.

Whether the vehicle's perception system failed to detect the duck, whether it detected but misclassified it as non-threatening, or whether it had another reason to continue unchanged is not established in the reporting.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
A self-driving car operated by Avride in Austin, Texas struck and killed a mother duck near Mueller Lake, prompting neighborhood frustration about autonomous vehicle safety. The duck, which had been nesting in a pot outside a local restaurant and was known to residents, was hit by the vehicle while in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. The vehicle did not slow down or stop after the incident. Local residents collected the duck's eggs and placed them in an incubator.

Following the incident and resident complaints, Avride reviewed vehicle data and found no evidence that the car failed to stop at a stop sign, contrary to one resident's claim. The company adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake from its service area. Avride stated it is now conducting simulations and controlled experiments to improve the technology and prevent similar situations, while ensuring these changes do not compromise the vehicle's overall safety performance.
